questions.q: What are the main functions of the judiciary, and why must it be independent?

answer.text: The judiciary is the system of courts that interprets and applies the law. It resolves disputes between citizens, between a citizen and the government, and between two governments. Through judicial review it can strike down laws that violate the Constitution, and it upholds the fundamental rights of citizens, who can approach it if their rights are denied.

For the judiciary to do this fairly, it must be independent — separated from the legislature and the executive, so that the government cannot influence its decisions. Only an independent judiciary can protect citizens against the misuse of state power and ensure that everyone, including the government, obeys the law.

questions.q: Describe the structure of the courts in India and the role of Public Interest Litigation.

answer.text: India has a single, integrated system of courts arranged like a pyramid. At the top is the Supreme Court in New Delhi, headed by the Chief Justice of India, whose decisions bind all other courts. Below it are the High Courts at the State level, and at the base are the district and subordinate courts. Cases can move upward on appeal.

Because courts can be costly and slow, from the 1980s the system of Public Interest Litigation, or PIL, allowed any person or group to approach the court on behalf of those whose rights are violated, sometimes through a simple letter. PIL has helped the poor and marginalised win justice on issues such as bonded labour and the environment.

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'rule of law', and how does it uphold equality before the law?

answer.text: means that all persons are equal before the law and that no one, however powerful, is above it — the same laws apply to everyone.

list: Every citizen, from an ordinary person to the highest official, is subject to the same law and courts
No one can be punished except for breaking a law, and only through a fair legal process
Laws are not arbitrary — they apply equally regardless of wealth, rank or religion

answer.text: is the foundation of democracy, protecting citizens from arbitrary power and ensuring justice and equality for all.

questions.q: How does the judicial system in India try to make justice accessible to the poor?

answer.text: is a right, but courts can be costly and slow, so several measures try to reach the disadvantaged.

list: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) lets any citizen or group approach the court on behalf of those who cannot themselves — even a letter can be treated as a petition
Legal aid provides free legal help to the poor
The courts have interpreted the right to life to include the right to shelter, food and a healthy environment

answer.text: widen access so that justice is not limited to those who can afford it, though delays and costs remain real challenges.
